findings.description: The inline policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:* and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", so the svc-deploy user has full control over every EC2 instance, S3 bucket/object, Lambda function and CloudWatch log in the account. This violates least privilege and enables account-wide data exfiltration, resource destruction, or service abuse (e.g. opening security groups via ec2:*) if the user's static credentials are ever compromised.

The output surfaces the svc-deploy access key secret material (encrypted_secret) and is not marked sensitive. Terraform outputs are persisted in state and, unless sensitive = true, printed in cleartext to CLI/CI logs, so access key material for an all-services IAM user can leak to anyone with log or state read access.

A static, non-expiring IAM access key is minted for a user holding wildcard permissions across EC2/S3/Lambda/CloudWatch. Such keys cannot be automatically rotated and act as a standing credential-stuffing/exfiltration target that grants broad access if leaked.
